statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-2005 (PostgreSQL pgcrypto heap buffer overflow executes arbitrary code) is fixed upstream in PostgreSQL 17.8: https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-2005/ lists 17.8 as the fixed release for major version 17, and the 17.8 release notes, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/17.8/, include it. Alpine's postgresql17 17.8-r0 is the upgrade to upstream 17.8 and lists CVE-2026-2005 under its secfixes: https://github.com/alpinelinux/aports/blob/ce22298320177ae25085d86fbf3b4fc1150c16a2/main/postgresql17/APKBUILD. The DHI postgresql17 packages for Alpine 3.23 are built from Alpine's postgresql17 APKBUILD at the aports revision for each package version (the current revision is linked above) and the upstream source release of the same version, and the postgres server binary in every published build (17.7-r0, 17.8-r0, 17.9-r0, 17.10-r0, 17.11-r0 and 17.12-r0), on both x86_64 and aarch64, reports the matching PostgreSQL 17 release. The pgcrypto module is present: pgcrypto.so ships in the postgresql17-contrib package of every published build for Alpine 3.23, on both x86_64 and aarch64. The earlier published build for Alpine 3.23 (17.7-r0) is built from an earlier upstream release and its server binary reports that older version, and Alpine applies no backport of this fix to it, so it is recorded as affected; 17.8-r0 and later carry the fix.

CVE-2026-2005 (PostgreSQL pgcrypto heap buffer overflow executes arbitrary code): a ciphertext provider can overflow the session key buffer in pgp_pub_decrypt_bytea(). https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-2005/ lists 18.2 as the fixed release for major version 18, and the 18.2 release notes, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/18.2/, list this CVE. The fix on the REL_18_STABLE branch is https://github.com/postgres/postgres/commit/209f387b81660e478eea147db9130af1d1c861f2 (Security: CVE-2026-2005, in tag REL_18_2 and not in REL_18_1), which adds a session key length check to contrib/pgcrypto/pgp-pubdec.c that logs 'incorrect session key length=%u' and returns a new error, 'Public key too big', which PostgreSQL 18.3 reworded to 'Session key too big'. Alpine's security database lists CVE-2026-2005 for postgresql18 under 18.2-r0. The DHI postgresql18 packages for Alpine 3.23 are built with Alpine's postgresql18 APKBUILD from the 3.23-stable branch of aports (current revision https://github.com/alpinelinux/aports/blob/59a1f1d230675807d5a95a0c1e57ba5d640ba039/main/postgresql18/APKBUILD) and the upstream PostgreSQL source release of the same version; none of the patches that APKBUILD applies, at any revision used for these builds, changes the files this fix changes. As of 2026-11-28 the DHI Alpine 3.23 package repository publishes builds of source postgresql18 at 18.1-r0, 18.2-r0, 18.3-r0, 18.4-r0, 18.6-r0 and 18.7-r0, for x86_64 and aarch64. We read every one of them on both architectures, with package checksums verified against the repository index, and in each the postgres server binary, /usr/libexec/postgresql18/postgres, reports the PostgreSQL release matching its package version. pgcrypto.so ships in the postgresql18-contrib package of every one of those builds on both architectures. The string 'incorrect session key length=%u' is in pgcrypto.so in 18.2-r0 and every later build and not in 18.1-r0, on both architectures, and it is not in the REL_18_1 source; 18.2-r0 also carries 'Public key too big', and 18.3-r0 and later carry 'Session key too big'. As a control, every build's pgcrypto.so contains the existing message 'Elgamal keys must be at least 1024 bits long'. 18.2-r0 is the first published build for Alpine 3.23 that carries the fix, and 18.2-r0, 18.3-r0, 18.4-r0, 18.6-r0 and 18.7-r0 carry it. The earlier published build (18.1-r0) is built from PostgreSQL releases before the fix and is affected.
